findings.title: A repeated X-CSRF-Token header is refused as a token failure
findings.detail: src/api/csrf.ts singleTokenHeader counts X-CSRF-Token occurrences in rawHeaders and treats anything other than exactly one occurrence as an absent token, so a request whose single logical token is correct is refused when the header is duplicated. No criterion scenario pins a repeated header; two reasonable implementations (first value wins, as parseCookies does for the session cookie, versus refuse) differ here.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a session POST carries two X-CSRF-Token headers THEN the PEP refuses it as CSRF token missing or invalid with payload reason token

findings.title: task 1.1: defineRoute throws ROUTE_AUTH_UNWIRED before the action checks, the reverse of the task's stated order
findings.detail: Task 1.1 says the first-failure order is (3) ROUTE_ACTION_MISSING then ROUTE_ACTION_UNKNOWN, then (4) ROUTE_AUTH_UNWIRED. In the committed src/api/route.ts the non-public block that throws ROUTE_AUTH_UNWIRED runs before the action checks, so a definition that fails both (an unwired non-session kind with no action) reports ROUTE_AUTH_UNWIRED where the task text says ROUTE_ACTION_MISSING. The scenario of C-d738ea05 (an hmac route with no action) matches the code, so no criterion is affected, but the task detail line is not done as written.

findings.title: task 3.1: the 503 raised for a missing PEP or a null pool/engine emits no warn line
findings.detail: Task 3.1 (and design.md) require that each 401 or 503 logs request.log.warn({ code, reason? }, "request refused"). In the authentication hook the early throw for no ursitoarePep, null pool or null engine leaves the function before any log call, so the AUTHZ_UNAVAILABLE answer of C-500709e4's first two situations is silent. Every other 401/503 path in the hook does log.

findings.title: task 4.1: the CSRF refusal is implemented in src/api/route.ts, not in an onRequest hook of src/api/pep.ts as the task text names it
findings.detail: Task 4.1 places the post-authentication CSRF check, the authz.csrf_refused audit and the CSRF_INVALID throw "in the onRequest hook of src/api/pep.ts". The committed src/api/pep.ts contains only installPep and decisionPreHandler; the logic lives in authenticationHook in src/api/route.ts (attached by defineRoute, as task 3.1 describes). Behaviour matches the specification scenarios, only the task's file detail is unfulfilled, and the two task texts disagree about where the hook lives.

findings.title: defineRoute after the instance has started records the route without registering it
findings.detail: defineRoute wraps server.route in try/catch and swallows FST_ERR_INSTANCE_ALREADY_LISTENING, then pushes the definition into state.defined regardless. A definition added after listen therefore appears in listDefinedRoutes (and is treated as covered) while no route exists and requests answer 404. No scenario pins this input down and reasonable implementations differ (throw vs. record).
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN defineRoute is called after the Fastify instance has started listening THEN the definition is recorded in listDefinedRoutes while server.route is skipped

findings.title: installPep rejects a public base URL that parses but carries credentials, a query or a fragment
findings.detail: parsePublicBaseUrl accepts only an http(s) origin with no username, password, search or hash; anything else is ROUTE_DEF_INVALID with reason public_base_url. The scenario only pins "not a url", so a base URL such as "https://app.example.com/?x=1" could reasonably have been accepted and reduced to its origin instead of being refused, and no criterion states which.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN publicBaseUrl parses as an http(s) URL but carries a username, password, query or fragment THEN installPep throws ROUTE_DEF_INVALID with details.reason public_base_url

findings.title: A repeated X-CSRF-Token header is refused as a token failure
findings.detail: src/api/csrf.ts singleTokenHeader counts X-CSRF-Token occurrences in rawHeaders and treats anything other than exactly one occurrence as an absent token, so a request whose single logical token is correct is refused when the header is duplicated. No criterion scenario pins a repeated header; two reasonable implementations (first value wins, as parseCookies does for the session cookie, versus refuse) differ here.

evidence.quote: if (count !== 1) { return undefined; } const value = request.headers["x-csrf-token"]; return typeof value === "string" ? value : undefined;

findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a session POST carries two X-CSRF-Token headers THEN the PEP refuses it as CSRF token missing or invalid with payload reason token

findings.title: task 1.1: defineRoute throws ROUTE_AUTH_UNWIRED before the action checks, the reverse of the task's stated order
findings.detail: Task 1.1 says the first-failure order is (3) ROUTE_ACTION_MISSING then ROUTE_ACTION_UNKNOWN, then (4) ROUTE_AUTH_UNWIRED. In the committed src/api/route.ts the non-public block that throws ROUTE_AUTH_UNWIRED runs before the action checks, so a definition that fails both (an unwired non-session kind with no action) reports ROUTE_AUTH_UNWIRED where the task text says ROUTE_ACTION_MISSING. The scenario of C-d738ea05 (an hmac route with no action) matches the code, so no criterion is affected, but the task detail line is not done as written.

findings.title: task 3.1: the 503 raised for a missing PEP or a null pool/engine emits no warn line
findings.detail: Task 3.1 (and design.md) require that each 401 or 503 logs request.log.warn({ code, reason? }, "request refused"). In the authentication hook the early throw for no ursitoarePep, null pool or null engine leaves the function before any log call, so the AUTHZ_UNAVAILABLE answer of C-500709e4's first two situations is silent. Every other 401/503 path in the hook does log.

findings.title: task 4.1: the CSRF refusal is implemented in src/api/route.ts, not in an onRequest hook of src/api/pep.ts as the task text names it
findings.detail: Task 4.1 places the post-authentication CSRF check, the authz.csrf_refused audit and the CSRF_INVALID throw "in the onRequest hook of src/api/pep.ts". findings.title: defineRoute after the instance has started records the route without registering it
findings.detail: defineRoute wraps server.route in try/catch and swallows FST_ERR_INSTANCE_ALREADY_LISTENING, then pushes the definition into state.defined regardless. A definition added after listen therefore appears in listDefinedRoutes (and is treated as covered) while no route exists and requests answer 404. No scenario pins this input down and reasonable implementations differ (throw vs. record).

evidence.quote: try { server.route(options); } catch (error) { if (!isAlreadyStarted(error)) { throw error; } } state.defined.push({ method: def.method, url: def.url, ... });

findings.suggested_fix: WHEN defineRoute is called after the Fastify instance has started listening THEN the definition is recorded in listDefinedRoutes while server.route is skipped

findings.title: installPep rejects a public base URL that parses but carries credentials, a query or a fragment
findings.detail: parsePublicBaseUrl accepts only an http(s) origin with no username, password, search or hash; anything else is ROUTE_DEF_INVALID with reason public_base_url. The scenario only pins "not a url", so a base URL such as "https://app.example.com/?x=1" could reasonably have been accepted and reduced to its origin instead of being refused, and no criterion states which.

evidence.quote: if ((parsed.protocol !== "http:" && parsed.protocol !== "https:") || parsed.username !== "" || parsed.password !== "" || parsed.search !== "" || parsed.hash !== "") { throw new RouteDefinitionError("ROUTE_DEF_INVALID", "Invalid public base URL", { reason: "public_base_url" }); }

findings.suggested_fix: WHEN publicBaseUrl parses as an http(s) URL but carries a username, password, query or fragment THEN installPep throws ROUTE_DEF_INVALID with details.reason public_base_url
